name: smooth-stream-text
description: Adaptive client-side pacing for streamed LLM text. Keep your Markdown renderer; the answer appears at an even rate. Zero-dependency headless core with React, Vue, Svelte and Web Component bindings and an optional fade-in reveal.

paragraphs: Adaptive text-stream smoothing for AI chat interfaces. Keep your existing Markdown renderer and pace incoming text with a zero-dependency headless core. React, Vue, Svelte and Web Component integrations are included; a fade-in reveal is optional.

When a language model answers, the chunks arrive unevenly: one word, then twenty at once, then a pause while the server thinks. Rendering each chunk the moment it lands means the text stutters, and the eye reads the stutter before it reads the words.

smooth-stream-text sits between your transport and your renderer. You hand it the text received so far and whether the answer is finished; it hands back a prefix that grows at an even, adaptive rate, which you render exactly as before. It works with any provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, your own backend) because it only sees text.
